observations.summary: White is a rigorous construction manual organized from parallel and angular perspective into oblique planes, shadows, cone of rays, and reflections; the back half is materially more technical than the already-held artist-facing foundation.

The early ground/picture-plane and plan/elevation material is strong but mostly reinforces established eye-level, scale-transfer, grid, plan-projection, curve-transfer, and level-reflection candidates.

White explicitly derives the measuring point for an arbitrary horizontal vanishing direction and supplies a geometric proof, strengthening D’Amelio’s existing measuring-line branch without needing a duplicate foundation card.
The oblique section adds exact metric handling of ascending/descending planes through plane vanishing lines and ascending/descending measuring points; this survives as a specialized new capability.
Sun and point-light basics overlap D’Amelio, but White materially deepens receiver handling when shadows cross inclined/vertical planes or land on curved surfaces.
The central-visual-ray/picture-plane model is useful, but White’s fixed 60-degree cone/1.5x-distance rule should not be promoted as a universal law before modern/mathematical reconciliation.
Vertical and tipped mirrors require reflected direction families derived from the mirror geometry, clearly generalizing the Norling level-plane reflection Pattern.
Gate 1 supports a mixed route: Review for most of the book, targeted strengthening patches, and Deep PASS only for oblique metric construction and general planar reflections.

rationale: White overlaps heavily with the cumulative foundation but contains two high-value technical deltas plus several exactness/receiver-model refinements that justify a complete Gate 2 read.
